verifyText.value: Relieve Financial Stress With Debt Consolidation

waitForText.value: Relieve Financial Stress With Debt Consolidation

verifyText.value: If you have multiple debts with high interest rates, debt consolidation can offer you the breathing room to get out of debt and organize your finances. A debt consolidation loan may help you reduce your interest rate, enjoy more affordable monthly payments, and pay off debt faster. Debt consolidation may also alleviate confusion over too many bills. A single payment with one due date is easier to track than multiple payments with different due dates.

If you are a homeowner, you may be able to use the equity you've built in your home for debt consolidation. The interest rate on a home equity loan is typically much lower than the interest rates on the debts being consolidated. Moreover, if you itemize deductions, interest paid on home equity debt is generally deductible for income tax purposes. If a home equity loan seems like the right approach for you, keep in mind that because you pledge your home as collateral, it could put your home ownership at risk if you are unable to make payments in the future. Also, even with a lower rate, depending on the term of the loan, you could actually spend more on interest over the life of the loan.
In addition to consolidating your debt, you may also consider the following strategies to get your finances back on track.
Knowledge is power. By monitoring where your money is going every month, you'll begin to make wiser choices.

Itemize your planned income and expenses for each month and compare your actual spending to see how things are going. If you find that you're often going over-budget in some areas out of necessity, you should consider cutting elsewhere to keep things under control.
Reigning in spending on non-essential items such as restaurant dining, premium cable, gourmet coffee, brand labels, etc., will free up more money for other areas of your budget and for savings.
Make extra cash to pay down debt by asking your boss for a raise, taking on more overtime, picking up a second job in the evenings and/or weekends, freelancing, sell clutter from your home, etc.
Contact each of your insurance providers to see how much increasing your deductible — the out of pocket amount you pay before insurance coverage on a claim begins — will reduce your insurance bill.

Along with your income and debt status, your personal credit profile can have a significant impact on which loans are available to you and the rates offered. A high credit rating can save you thousands of dollars over the life of a loan.
Individuals with excellent credit ratings typically have a FICO score above 740
Individuals with good credit ratings typically have a FICO score between 660 and 740
Individuals with fair credit ratings typically have a FICO score between 580 and 660
Individuals with poor credit ratings typically have a FICO score below 580
A FICO score is comprised of 5 parts:

Your types of accounts and your payment record; any bankruptcies, legal judgments, wage garnishments, etc.; the severity and amount of late payments; the number of past-due items and when they occurred. (35%)
How much you currently owe and on what types of accounts; number of accounts with balances; the proportion of credit lines still available. (30%)
Time since accounts opened; by specific type of account; since last activity. (15%)
Number of recently opened accounts, by type and date opened; recent credit inquiries and date of inquiries; reestablishment of good credit after payment delinquencies. (10%)
The number and types of credit accounts available for your use. (10%)
By federal law, you're entitled to a free credit report once every 12 months from each of the three major credit bureaus - Experian, TransUnion, or Equifax.
